notes: All required searches have now run: 8 web searches across two runs (6 in the first run on 11 November 2026; in that run the search on extinction or existential risk was refused, and it was run successfully in a second run the same day, plus one follow-up). The extinction or existential risk search returned coverage of the September 2026 congressional debate on AI extinction warnings (naming Kelly, Cruz, Sanders and others) but no result mentioning Schmitt. The follow-up checked whether he is attached to the catastrophic-risk AI bill that Cruz said he was drafting with Thune and Klobuchar: no source names Schmitt as a co-sponsor, the bill text had reportedly not been released as of mid-September 2026, and the only mention of him was an advocacy post noting he sits on the Commerce Committee. Neither search produced a statement by him, so no pages from them were opened and nothing was added. Also in the first run I opened the official site's press release list (latest 10, 18 Sep to 9 Nov 2026: none about AI) and the site's own search for 'artificial intelligence' (12 results, 6 from 2025-2026: defense bills, a science foundation award, Medicare fraud; none titled as AI risk; only the 16 May 2025 release was opened). Not on the verified signer list of the 23 September 2026 China letter, so he did not sign. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: no source found showing him as a co-sponsor; the Sanders summary PDF could not be read as text, so co-sponsorship is unconfirmed rather than ruled out by a sponsor list. Quote caveats: the two Startland News quotes were read through a page-fetch tool that summarises pages; a second fetch confirmed each as one uninterrupted quotation, but I could not download the raw page (site blocked a direct download), so a reviewer should check them character for character, including the apostrophe style (curly vs straight). The event date 2025-10-14 is inferred from the article (published Thursday 16 October 2025, event 'Tuesday'). The 16 May 2025 quote was checked against the raw page text. Left out: other Startland quotes that the fetch tool truncated (including one beginning "It’s probably important for the federal government to come in and preempt this,"). Out of date range and not included: a 2023 Fox News interview after a classified AI briefing where he reportedly called the threat 'very existential because China's playing for keeps' (about China's military threat, not risk from AI itself; seen only in a search result). The search for 'AI safety' returned only results about Eric Schmidt, the former Google chief executive, a different person.
